caption:
Quinn's check-up showed blood pressure on the high side, so Quinn planned to never move again — especially not with weights.

Kay's take: regular exercise is one of the most helpful habits for blood pressure, and sensible strength training is usually fine too.

What can help: around 150 minutes of moderate cardio a week (walking, cycling, swimming), strength work two to three times a week, breathing through each lift instead of holding your breath, and building up gradually using how hard it feels.

If your blood pressure is very high or newly found, or you have heart or kidney conditions, check in with your GP first. Chest pain, palpitations, unusual breathlessness, dizziness or fainting during exercise mean stop and get help.
